## Summary

I demonstrated reach direction and velocity tuning in primary motor cortex using Dandiset [000129](https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/000129) (MC_RTT: macaque M1 spiking during self-paced reaching), streamed directly from DANDI S3 via `remfile`. The session has 130 M1 units and 1 kHz cursor kinematics during 545 continuous, self-paced reaches.

Using two independent methods — continuous velocity-based tuning curves (cosine-fit, à la Georgopoulos) and discrete per-reach direction binning keyed to target-acquisition events — I found strong, pervasive directional tuning (83/130 units R²>0.3, up to R²=0.91) and speed tuning (99/130 units |ρ|>0.5, mostly positive). The two methods agreed well (median 18° preferred-direction offset), and a peri-reach raster for the best-tuned unit visually confirmed ~2.5x rate modulation across direction quadrants.

Deliverables in the working directory:
- `reach_direction_velocity_tuning.py` — jupytext script (runs end-to-end)
- `reach_direction_velocity_tuning.ipynb` — executed notebook, no errors
- `fig1`–`fig8` PNGs — raw data validation, kinematics, direction/speed tuning curves, population summaries, cross-method validation, and direction-split rasters
- `README.md` — dataset, methods, and findings summary
